title: check-init
summary: Answers whether a variable or field is set before a given use on every execution (SET / NEVER-SET / MAY-BE-UNSET)
intro: Ask it before adding an Assigned guard or reordering initialization: it names the writers of a unit variable, class var or field and says whether one of them runs before the use on every path. Exit 0 = all SET, 1 = some MAY-BE-UNSET or NEVER-SET, 2 = error. Internal until the 1.52 engine lanes land.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Analyze > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
steps: Put the caret on a unit variable, class var or field (a use of it) in the code editor
Choose drag-lint > Analyze > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
The Messages window shows the verdict (SET / NEVER-SET / MAY-BE-UNSET / UNKNOWN-CALLEE), one line per judged use with its witness hops, and one line per writer; double-click a line to jump there

surfaces.caption: drag-lint > Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
steps: Right-click on a variable or field in the code editor
Open the drag-lint submenu and choose Check Initialization of Identifier at Cursor...
Read the verdict, uses, witness hops and writers in the Messages window; double-click a line to jump there

questions.ask: Is this variable set before it is read here, on every execution?
Which routines or events set this field?
